engine.meaning: The original, unchanged in substance; every point survives.
engine.sense: The one swap fits: "especially if you have heaps of cookies set".
engine.authenticity: Essentially no Aussie, and US spelling left beside UK spelling: "issue a personalized or generic response" and "**Personalization**" next to "Recording and analysing user behaviour".
engine.register: Untranslated apart from spelling and "heaps"; far under level 2.
engine.tone: The original's neutral documentation tone, unchanged.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every technical point survives: storing, creating, modifying, sending back; the four sign-in steps; the three uses; the limits; the Set-Cookie headers. "which matters cos" makes the original's implied link explicit, faithfully.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Every term fits: "The browser can hang onto cookies", "If the credentials check out", "to say it reckons the user's still signed in", "the modern storage APIs are the go", "To have a squiz at stored cookies".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian developer explaining it: "These days the modern storage APIs are the go", "Storage APIs can hold way more data".
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, even Aussie layer right for level 2, without touching the code or terms; no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the clear, neutral explanatory tone, just more relaxed: "Here's how a basic user sign-in system goes:"
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Once it's got an HTTP request, a server can send one or more".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "hang onto", "check out", "reckons", "the go", "squiz", "way more", "heaps", "what users get up to".

unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact ("it still reckons the user is signed in", "drag down performance"), but "out of the box, the HTTP protocol is" shifts 'by default' towards product-setup sense, and "shopping trolley contents" is odd for a website.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural and plain, with a few local touches: "Recording and analysing what users get up to"; "shopping trolley" for a web cart is a localisation an Australian would notice.
unharnessed.register: Light for level 2: plain English with "reckons", "what users get up to", "have a look".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Cookies get sent with every request, so they can drag down performance".

yarn-troppo.meaning: The technical content survives, but it adds commentary and claims: "Yep, that's the one people worry about.", "which is where it gets interesting", "usually 4KB, which is tiny", "out in the sticks".
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits ("the session ID gets binned", "earn their keep"), but the cookie joke plays on the wrong sense of cookie: "Ever hear the one about the cookie you can't dunk in your cuppa?"
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much is natural Aussie, but some lines are bolted on: "Ever hear the one about", "Memory like a goldfish, by default.", "Choccy and strawberry, no less".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2: jokes and similes on most paragraphs, "simple as", "'em", "have a squiz"; no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The neutral reference tone becomes jokey, and the tracking line editorialises: "Like a stamp on the back of your hand at the door."
yarn-troppo.flow: Readable, but asides interrupt the technical sequence: "basically going "Still me, still signed in, reckon.""
yarn-troppo.variety: Very varied: "squiz", "binned", "stash", "whip up", "fiddle with", "earn their keep", "out in the sticks".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the article, but its plain reference character is buried under banter.

yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "it still reckons the user is signed in", "if you've got heaps of cookies set", "to work out whether".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural plain Australian English, but very little local colour; "shopping cart" and stiff carry-overs like "Modern storage APIs are now recommended".
yarn-deadset.register: Light for level 2: little beyond "reckons", "heaps", "work out".
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth: "Cookies are sent with every request, so they can slow things down".

summaries.engine: The original with a few spelling changes and one 'heaps'.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: The best: accurate, natural and light, with Aussie idiom that never touches the technical sense.
summaries.unharnessed: Faithful plain-English version with a light Aussie touch, lighter than asked.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and varied, but over-embellished for level 2, turning reference docs into banter with added claims.
summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful, smooth version with a very light Aussie touch, lighter than asked.
